subject: pe
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: Skills in isolation and competitive situations

questions.q: What is a 'closed skill'?
options: A skill performed in a predictable, stable environment
A skill that can only be performed by professionals
A skill performed against strong opposition
A skill that always uses the whole body
questions.explain: Closed skills are self-paced and take place in a settled, predictable environment such as a free throw or a golf swing.

questions.q: What does performing a skill 'in isolation' mean?
options: Performing the skill in an unopposed drill or practice
Performing the skill only during a full match
Performing the skill blindfolded
Performing the skill as part of a team relay
questions.explain: In isolation, a skill is demonstrated in a controlled drill without opposition, allowing the technique itself to be assessed.

questions.q: Which of these is an 'open skill'?
options: A dribble in a football match
A gymnastics vault
A trampoline routine
A javelin throw
questions.explain: Open skills are affected by an unpredictable, changing environment, such as dribbling past opponents in a match.

questions.q: A skill that is simple and requires little concentration or decision-making is best described as a:
options: Basic skill
Complex skill
Closed loop
Tactical skill
questions.explain: Basic (simple) skills require little thought or decision-making, whereas complex skills demand greater concentration and judgement.

questions.q: In goal setting, what does the 'M' in SMART stand for?
options: Measurable
Motivating
Mental
Maximal
questions.explain: SMART targets are Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Realistic and Time-bound.

questions.q: When analysing a performance, a 'strength' is:
options: An aspect the performer does well
An aspect the performer needs to improve
A rule the performer has broken
A tactic used by the opposition
questions.explain: A strength is a component of performance carried out effectively, whereas a weakness is an area needing improvement.

questions.q: The main purpose of the rules of an activity is to:
options: Ensure the activity is fair and safe
Guarantee the home team always wins
Increase the number of spectators
Make the game last longer
questions.explain: Rules (laws/regulations) govern play so that competition is fair and participants are kept safe.

questions.q: Which official is responsible for enforcing the rules during a game of football?
options: The referee
The captain
The physiotherapist
The manager
questions.explain: The referee applies the laws of the game and makes decisions on infringements during play.

questions.q: Why is a skill often performed more successfully in isolation than in a competitive situation?
options: There is no opposition or pressure to disrupt the performer
The rules are different in isolation
The performer is allowed more attempts in a match
Isolation practice always uses better equipment
questions.explain: Without opponents, decision-making demands or pressure, the performer can focus purely on technique.

questions.q: A netball centre pass made while being marked is an open skill mainly because:
options: The environment is unpredictable and affected by opponents
It is a self-paced movement
It never involves decision-making
It is always performed the same way
questions.explain: Open skills must be adapted to a changing environment, such as the position and movement of markers.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of analysing a sporting performance?
options: To identify strengths and weaknesses so performance can be improved
To decide the final score of the match
To choose the team captain
To set the price of tickets
questions.explain: Analysis breaks down a performance to highlight what is done well and what needs developing, informing improvement.

questions.q: How does 'evaluation' differ from 'analysis' of performance?
options: Evaluation judges the quality and suggests improvements, analysis breaks it down
Evaluation only counts the goals scored
Analysis is done by the coach, evaluation by spectators
There is no difference between them
questions.explain: Analysis identifies the components of performance, while evaluation makes a judgement on their quality and recommends action.

questions.q: What is the difference between a 'strategy' and a 'tactic'?
options: A strategy is the overall plan; tactics are the specific actions used to carry it out
A strategy applies only to individuals; tactics only to teams
A tactic lasts a whole season; a strategy lasts one match
They mean exactly the same thing
questions.explain: A strategy is the broad game plan, whereas tactics are the specific manoeuvres used to implement it.

questions.q: Why might a team choose to use a defensive tactic when winning late in a game?
options: To protect their lead and reduce the risk of conceding
To break the rules without being caught
To increase the number of players allowed on the pitch
To make the referee's job easier
questions.explain: Defensive tactics limit opponents' scoring opportunities, helping a team preserve an advantage.

questions.q: A complex skill differs from a basic skill because it:
options: Requires greater concentration, judgement and decision-making
Can never be performed in a match
Is only used in warm-ups
Uses no muscles
questions.explain: Complex skills involve more information processing and decision-making than simple, basic skills.

questions.q: A badminton player practises the same overhead clear repeatedly against a wall with no opponent. This is an example of:
options: A skill performed in isolation
A skill performed in a competitive situation
An open skill
A tactical decision
questions.explain: Repeating the shot in an unopposed drill assesses the technique in isolation rather than in competition.

questions.q: A football team is losing 1-0 with ten minutes left. Which tactic is most appropriate?
options: Push more players forward to attack and try to equalise
Keep all players in defence to protect the score
Deliberately give away fouls to waste time
Substitute the goalkeeper for a defender
questions.explain: When behind late in a game, committing players forward increases attacking opportunities to score.

questions.q: A coach notes a swimmer has excellent stroke technique but a slow reaction off the blocks. In an analysis, the slow start should be recorded as a:
options: Weakness to be improved
Strength to maintain
Rule infringement
Tactic
questions.explain: The slow start is an area of underperformance, so it is classed as a weakness needing improvement.

questions.q: A netballer sets the target: 'Increase my shooting accuracy from 60% to 75% within eight weeks.' Which SMART principle makes this target 'Time-bound'?
options: The eight-week deadline
The mention of shooting
The 75% figure
The reference to accuracy
questions.explain: A time-bound target has a clear deadline, here provided by the eight-week timeframe.

questions.q: A tennis player performs a serve at the start of a point with no interference from the environment. How is this skill best classified?
options: A closed skill
An open skill
A tactic
A rule
questions.explain: The serve is self-paced and performed in a stable, predictable environment, making it a closed skill.

specSource: Pearson Edexcel GCSE PE & Sport Science (1PE0) specification; Practical Performance
